page: Microsoft Azure F48als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a 48-core dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture at 3.7 GHz, providing 48 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-physical-core ratio. The instance is paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The underlying AMD processor supports extended instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions), AES, and SHA_NI. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage drives, requiring external remote volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution capabilities, driven by the dedicated 48-core processor. The instance achieves top 10% ratings in multi-core metrics, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 147,786.21, a Geekbench multi-core score of 24,068.0, and a Clang compilation score of 64,381.0. Extended instruction throughput is also strong, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 105,207.72. Memory throughput remains robust across large blocks, recording 226.93 GB/sec for uncached reads and 144.12 GB/sec for writes.

From an operational and cost-efficiency perspective, the F48als_v6 focuses resource expenditure strictly on high-density compute power. By maintaining a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio and omitting onboard storage, it maximizes raw compute yield per allocated resource without incurring costs for unneeded memory or local NVMe pools. Workloads requiring extreme in-memory datasets or low-latency local disks may face bottlenecks, but applications prioritizing multi-threaded compute density benefit from the dedicated core allocation.

The instance is best suited for compute-heavy workloads such as large-scale software compilation, batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, video encoding, and multi-threaded data transformations.

The instance omits local storage and dedicated GPUs, routing primary I/O to remote volumes. Hardware support includes AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the F48als_v6 delivers top-tier parallel compute, demonstrating top 10% performance in multi-core stress tests, Geekbench multi-core execution, and software compilation via Clang. It maintains strong memory bandwidth, reaching 226.93 GB/sec on uncached reads. This compute-centric configuration is best suited for build servers, multi-threaded simulation, continuous integration pipelines, and CPU-bound batch workloads.
